Class Game

java.lang.Object
Game
public class Game extends Object
This file acts as the central game engine and state manager. It initializes the world (goods, ports, and the merchant), tracks the progression of time (days), handles the core logic for traveling, and evaluates the win/loss conditions to determine when the game ends.

    • Game

      public Game(String name, int capital, double targetProfit)
      Creates a new game starting on Day 0. The merchant starts in Manila with an empty vessel, and Manila's prices are then generated.
      Parameters:
      name - the merchant's name
      capital - the starting capital in gold
      targetProfit - the target profit percentage

    • travel

      public boolean travel(Port dest)
      When sailing to another port one turn passes and the day rises by one. The merchant then docks at the destination and the destination generates new prices. The last allowed journey lands on day getMaxTurns().
      Parameters:
      dest - the destination port
      Returns:
      true if the journey occurred, false if the game is over wherein the destination is equal to null, the destination is not one of of the game's ports, or the destination is the merchant's current port.

    • isGameOver

      public boolean isGameOver()
      Checks whether the game has ended by attaining the target or by the turn limit being met. (Note: Quitting is handled by the console driver)
      Returns:
      true if the profit percentage has been met or if the day (turn) limit has been reached

    • getEndMessage

      public String getEndMessage()
      Creates an end of the game (final) message that summarizes the game's outcome. In so it displays whether the merchant has won, ran out of time, or quit, followed by the merchant's final gold, total profit, and the number of days taken to attain such.
      Returns:
      the end of the game message to print
